note: Nomination-day report for the fourteen divisions of Newry No. 1 (County Down) rural district, one member each. There was no contest; Mr. Pierce P. Fegan took Carrickcrossan in place of Mr. James Gorman, who retired, and four retiring members (Messrs. J. M'Connell, P. M'Ateer, A. J. M'Clean and E. J. Convery) were not nominated but continued as members; their divisions are inferred from the 1927 return. Sole nomination; returned unopposed. Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Corrected from the page image of Newry Telegraph, 3 May 1930, p. 2 (council-audit, Nov 2026): citation moved from the Newry Reporter, 3 May 1930, p. 2 (whose link led to that issue's masthead, and whose issue has no Newry No. 1 list) to the Newry Telegraph report that prints the list. Renamed from 'Clonallon' to Clonallan (19 Nov 2026, w19-tidy, the owner's decision 4 of 19 Nov 2026: a division filed under two spellings takes its official name, and each round keeps the spelling it was filed under as Constituency_Name_As_Printed): the Northern Ireland DED maps of 1925-69 name the DED Clonallan; the rounds were filed as Clonallon (1927, 1930, 1933, 1936, 1946, 1949, 1952, 1955, 1958, 1961, 1964, 1967); Clonallion (1939). This round was filed as 'Clonallon', kept as Constituency_Name_As_Printed; the old address (clonallon) answers with a redirect to this one.
